title: Canonical Rees reduction identifies the two closed fibres
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $I,J\subseteq A$ be ideals. Use affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Write $R_A(J)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}J^nt^n$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra], $\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)=\operatorname{Proj}R_A(J)$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup], and use scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose that the canonical maps induced by $f$ give ring isomorphisms $e_0:A/I\simeq B/IB$ and $e_R:R_A(J)/IR_A(J)\simeq R_B(JB)/(IB)R_B(JB)$: explicitly, each isomorphism sends every residue class to the residue class of its canonical image. Then there is an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Bl}_{JB}(\operatorname{Spec}B)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}B}\operatorname{Spec}(B/IB)\simeq\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Its composite with the first projection is the first projection followed by the canonical blowup morphism induced by $f$; its composite with the second projection is the second projection followed by $\operatorname{Spec}(e_0)$. No finite-generation, flatness or completion hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The extended ideal IR_A(J) is homogeneous: its degree-n component is IJ^n. The coefficientwise map induced by f respects the grading and the extended ideals, so it descends to a graded map of the two quotient Rees rings. The representative formula identifies its underlying ring map with e_R. A bijective graded map has graded inverse: decompose a preimage into its finitely many homogeneous components and use injectivity to make all components outside the target degree zero. The degree-zero map agrees with e_0, by the representative formulas.

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-base-change-arbitrary] to the Rees graded algebra over Spec A and the quotient morphism Spec(A/I) -> Spec A, and likewise over B. On every affine open, the pullback algebra is the original graded algebra tensored with the residue ring; the map x tensor a-bar -> a*x identifies it with the homogeneous quotient by I. Thus the closed fibres identify with Proj of the quotient Rees graded rings. The graded isomorphism in Step 1 identifies those Proj schemes over Spec(e_0). Compose the two base-change isomorphisms with this isomorphism.

proof.text: On a standard homogeneous localization the constructed morphism sends F/s^d to f(F)/f(s)^d. After the first projection this is exactly the morphism of blowups induced by f. On degree-zero constants the map is e_0, giving the second projection formula. These formulas agree on chart intersections because they are induced by the same coefficientwise homomorphism; the standard charts cover Proj, so both identities hold globally. If the quotient graded ring is zero the Proj schemes are empty and the identities still hold; if J is the unit ideal the assertion reduces to Spec(e_0).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_closedFiberIso_of_reesReduction
    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    (f : A →+* B) (I J : Ideal A)
    (e₀ : A ⧸ I ≃+* B ⧸ I.map f)
    (he₀ : ∀ a : A, e₀ (Ideal.Quotient.mk I a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (f a))
    (eR : reesAlgebra J ⧸ I.map (algebraMap A (reesAlgebra J)) ≃+*
      reesAlgebra (J.map f) ⧸ (I.map f).map (algebraMap B (reesAlgebra (J.map f))))
    (heR : ∀ F : reesAlgebra J,
      eR (Ideal.Quotient.mk _ F) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (reesGrading.hom f rfl F)) :
    ∃ e : pullback (AffineBlowup.toSpec (J.map f))
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map f)))) ≅
        pullback (AffineBlowup.toSpec J)
          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))),
      e.hom ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = pullback.fst _ _ ≫ AffineBlowup.hom f rfl ∧
      e.hom ≫ pullback.snd _ _ = pullback.snd _ _ ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom e₀.toRingHom)
